title: Thinking-in-Bets at Test Time Reduces Sycophantic Revisions in LLM Agents
abstract: arXiv:2610.34654v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Language model agents often abandon correct work when a user challenges it, yet simply telling them to stand firm makes them ignore real mistakes. Once an agent reads a complaint, it tends to discount its own earlier checks in order to agree with the user. We introduce Thinking-in-Bets, a training-free method in which an agent writes a short private record of its main claims, the checks supporting them, and its confidence before reading user feedback. When challenged, the agent consults this Claim Checklist to keep verified work intact while investigating uncertain or newly challenged parts. We evaluate five Gemini models (3.5 Flash-Lite, 3.5 Flash, 3.6 Flash, 3.8 Flash, and 4.0 Argon) across eight benchmarks: SWE-Together, SWE-Interact, and DeepSWE for software engineering, Agents' Last Exam for professional reports, Humanity's Last Exam and SycEval for academic reasoning, Vals Finance for financial analysis, and Terminal-Bench for co

translated_title: 测试时押注式思考减少大语言模型智能体的谄媚性修改
translated_abstract: 语言模型智能体在用户质疑其工作时常常放弃原本正确的结果，但简单地告诉它们坚持立场又会使它们忽视真正的错误。一旦智能体读到用户的抱怨，它往往为了迎合用户而低估自己之前的检查。我们提出了押注式思考，这是一种无需训练的方法：智能体在阅读用户反馈之前，先写下一份简短的私密记录，包含其主要论断、支持这些论断的检查依据以及自身的置信度。当受到质疑时，智能体会参考这份“论断清单”，在保持已验证工作完整的同时，去调查不确定的或新受到质疑的部分。我们在八个基准上评估了五个Gemini模型（3.5 Flash-Lite、3.5 Flash、3.6 Flash、3.8 Flash和4.0 Argon）：软件工程领域的SWE-Together、SWE-Interact和DeepSWE，专业报告领域的Agents' Last Exam，学术推理领域的Humanity's Last Exam和SycEval，金融分析领域的Vals Finance，以及终端任务的Terminal-Bench。
tldr: 提出无需训练的“押注式思考”方法，让智能体在读取用户反馈前先私密记录其论断、验证依据与置信度，从而在受到质疑时保护已验证的成果、减少LLM智能体的谄媚性修改。
en_tdlr: Thinking-in-Bets is a training-free method where an agent privately records its main claims, supporting checks, and confidence before reading user feedback, enabling it to preserve verified work under challenge and thereby reduce sycophantic revisions in LLM agents.
